meta.name: CATSKILLS-SSTO
meta.description: Pure geometry / topology assembly. Drop-in modules mate at named ports.
meta.architecture: Drop-ins each with own skid and bay doors: cargo, Fusion electric plant, combined-cycle engine. Plant ↔ engine by power cable (DEC → bus coupler). Tail bolts to fuselage around the engine nozzle cutout; nozzle belongs to the engine only.
meta.skids: Cargo, Fusion power plant, and combined-cycle engine are separate drop-in packages.

children.label: Fuselage
children.note: Structural boat: open cradle plus the pieces that permanently live on it — nose landing gear and the two aft space-steering pods. Forward steering is on the crew capsule, not here. Includes the Shuttle-style body flap on the aft belly.

children.label: Fuselage cradle
children.note: Open boat / long cradle. Drop-in wells for crew, airlock, cargo bay, CHARM power plant, and combined-cycle engine. Belly wing saddle + nose-gear saddle. Aft steering pods bolt to this cradle; forward steering rides on the crew capsule.

ports.note: Open forward well for crew capsule drop-in
Open mid-body well; Cargo Bay (skid+doors) drops in as one unit
Open well for Fusion electric plant drop-in (~33.3–45 m)
Open aft well for combined-cycle engine drop-in (~45–52 m, with water + tail)
Belly saddle / pinch for one-piece wing
Local saddle / dimple in the fuselage cradle belly. Nose landing gear bolts up into this hardpoint (same idea as the wing saddle, smaller).
Aft hardpoint for vertical stabilizer. Bolts around the engine nozzle cutout — nozzle pokes out underneath; Tail does not attach to the nozzle.
Body flap hinge on aft cradle belly

children.label: Nose landing gear
children.note: Isolated nose wheel. Bolts to a saddle/dimple on the fuselage cradle belly — not buried in a closed well as primary structure language.

children.label: Left aft steering pod
children.placement: aft fuselage, left of tail fin (Shuttle OMS/RCS pod)
children.note: Shuttle-style left aft OMS/RCS pod; bolts to fuselage cradle.

children.label: Right aft steering pod
children.placement: aft fuselage, right of tail fin (Shuttle OMS/RCS pod)
children.note: Shuttle-style right aft OMS/RCS pod; bolts to fuselage cradle.

children.label: Body flap
children.note: Shuttle-style single body flap on the aft fuselage belly — pitch trim and engine-bell thermal shield on entry. Hinged to the fuselage cradle, not part of the Tail assembly.

children.label: Crew capsule
children.note: Drop-in collection: pressure vessel (with interior) plus side hatch and forward steering module bolted to the vessel. Drops into the forward cradle well.

children.label: Pressure vessel
children.note: Physical pressurized shell of the crew capsule. Holds flight deck and living cabin. Side hatch and forward steering module bolt onto this vessel; they are siblings in the capsule collection, not interior furnishings.

ports.note: Nose hardpoint on pressure vessel for forward steering module

children.label: Left-side ground hatch (runway only)
children.note: Left-side ground hatch cut into the pressure-vessel skin. Runway ingress only — not vacuum-rated as an outer space hatch.

children.label: Forward steering module (nose)
children.note: Hedgehog of small space-steering jets on the pressure-vessel nose (Crew Dragon–style). Bolts to the vessel; not inside the pressurized volume.

children.label: Airlock
children.note: Drop-in collection: pressure vessel (suited standing room) plus the two pressure doors, air tank, and pressurization gadgets. Hatches only to crew and cargo — submarine / ISS style.

children.label: Pressure vessel
children.note: Suited standing chamber (~2 people). Physical pressurized shell of the airlock. Doors, air tank, and cycle gadgets bolt to this vessel.

children.label: Door between cabin and airlock
children.note: Pressure door on the forward face of the airlock pressure vessel (crew side).

children.label: Door between airlock and cargo bay
children.note: Pressure door on the aft face of the airlock pressure vessel (cargo-bay side).

children.label: Air tank (press / depress)
children.note: Stores air to repressurize the chamber after vacuum; accepts dump/bleed during depress.

children.label: Pressurization gadgets
children.note: Valves, pump/equalizer, gauges, and controls to pressurize and unpressurize the chamber (ISS / submarine airlock style).

children.label: Cargo bay
children.note: Drop-in collection: cargo skid plus its own left/right doors. The fuselage cradle is open here — doors are not fuselage skin; they come with the bay.

children.label: Cargo skid
children.note: Pull-out cargo skid — the physical cargo bay. Doors hinge to this skid; skid sits in the fuselage cradle well. No pressure door aft — EVA into the open CHARM / engine wells for maintenance.

children.label: Fusion electric plant
children.note: Drop-in electric power plant: fusion plant skid (structure + bay doors) plus battery, p/¹¹B fuel, CHARM, DEC, and island auxiliaries. Separate cradle from the combined-cycle engine; linked mainly by a power cable.

children.label: Fusion plant skid
children.note: Collection: skid structure plus its left/right bay doors. Expand to see doors; plant equipment lives on the Fusion electric plant beside this skid.

children.label: Skid structure
children.note: Physical drop-in frame. Bay doors hinge here; plant equipment bolts here. Sits in the fuselage cradle well.

children.label: Left fusion plant bay door
children.note: Hinged to fusion plant skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Right fusion plant bay door
children.note: Hinged to fusion plant skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Fusion fuel tanks (proton / boron-11)
children.note: Proton / boron-11 feed for CHARM.

children.label: CHARM
children.note: Chambered Aneutronic Rotating Mirror core (multi-chamber string). Ordered alphas → DEC. Not a thruster.

children.label: DEC
children.note: Direct energy conversion. Plant electrical product. Power cable to propulsion bus coupler starts here.

ports.note: Electrical bus feed — power cable to propulsion bus coupler

children.label: Mirror magnets + PSU
children.note: CHARM island magnets and power supplies (paper plant schematic).

children.label: RF units
children.note: RF / ponderomotive wall drivers for CHARM chambers.

children.label: Cryo + coolant bath
children.note: Cryogenics and coolant bath for the fusion island.

children.label: Combined-cycle engine
children.note: Drop-in: engine skid (structure + bay doors) plus water tanks and propulsion hardware. Power from Fusion electric plant via cable (DEC → bus coupler). Nozzle clears under Tail; Tail is a separate fuselage-mounted assembly.

children.label: Engine skid
children.note: Collection: skid structure plus its left/right bay doors. Expand to see doors; propulsion hardware lives on the Combined-cycle engine beside this skid.

children.label: Skid structure
children.note: Physical drop-in propulsion frame. Bay doors hinge here; engine hardware bolts here. Sits in the aft fuselage cradle well. Nozzle exits under Tail.

ports.note: Receives CHARM DEC bus via power cable

children.label: Left engine bay door
children.note: Hinged to combined-cycle engine skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Right engine bay door
children.note: Hinged to combined-cycle engine skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Water tanks (space propellant)
children.note: Carried water = R3 reaction mass. Lives on the engine drop-in (not the CHARM plant). Fed to the water injector; ionized in the engine.

children.label: Shared exhaust nozzle
children.note: Combined-cycle exhaust. Pokes aft under the Tail assembly / through the cradle tail cutout. Tail bolts to the fuselage around this nozzle; Tail does not own or joint to the nozzle.

children.label: Water injector
children.note: Meters carried water into the thruster for R3 (vacuum). Fed from water tanks.

children.label: Water ionizer / plasma accelerator
children.note: Where water is ionized and accelerated for the water-plasma jet (R3). Bus power → exhaust kinetic energy. Not part of the CHARM chamber string.

children.label: Propulsion bus coupler
children.note: Engine-side end of the CHARM power cable / bus. Feeds fan, heater, MHD, and water-ionizer modes.

children.label: Tail assembly
Vertical stabilizer
children.note: Physical fin. Roots to fuselage cradle around the engine nozzle clearance. No joint to the nozzle — the nozzle belongs to the combined-cycle engine.

children.label: Left rudder / speed-brake panel
children.note: Shuttle-style split rudder panel. Together with the right panel: same deflection = yaw; open like a book = speed brake.

children.label: Right rudder / speed-brake panel
children.note: Shuttle-style split rudder panel. Together with the left panel: same deflection = yaw; open like a book = speed brake.
Vertical stabilizer + split rudder panels. Bolted to the fuselage cradle around the top of the engine nozzle opening. Does not own or connect to the nozzle.

children.label: Wing
children.note: Collection: mono-wing body, elevons, and main landing gear. The physical wing bolts to the fuselage cradle belly saddle.

children.label: Mono-wing body
children.note: Single left–right wing structure / wing box.

ports.note: Wing body upper face → fuselage belly saddle

children.label: Left elevon
children.note: Shuttle-style elevon (combined roll/pitch). Trailing edge of left wing.

children.label: Right elevon
children.note: Shuttle-style elevon (combined roll/pitch). Trailing edge of right wing.

children.label: Main landing gear
children.note: Optional sub-kit: left and right main gear joined as one assembly, then mated to the wing mount points — or each leg mated alone. Shuttle mains live in the wing, not the fuselage belly.
